raw_response:
I am seventy years old. I have been working this land for fifty years. My wife and I live together, our children work in the city. Thirteen mu is a lot of work for two old people, but we manage. I will tell you what I will do this year, same as most years.

**Wheat first, because I already planted it last October.**

I sowed the wheat in early October, right after I harvested the maize. I used the improved seed the shop in town sells — everyone around here uses it, I cannot remember the name but the bag is yellow. I bought about 15 jin per mu, maybe a little more because my soil is not soft enough and some seed does not come up.

Before sowing I spread the base fertilizer. I used compound fertilizer, two bags per mu, one bag is 50 jin. That gives nitrogen and phosphorus and a little potassium all together. I also spread some pig manure we saved, about half a cart per mu on the fields closer to the house.

Now in spring, when the wheat starts standing up (jointing time), I will spread urea. I use one bag per mu, 40 jin. My neighbor Old Wang uses a little less but he always complains his wheat is yellow, so I do not listen to him. Better to put enough. Wheat is our food and also money.

I will water the wheat at winter (already done in December when ground was freezing) and again at jointing when I put the urea, and one more time when the grain is filling. Three waters. The well is close, the pump still works.

For pests, I will spray once for aphids around April, and once more with the herbicide mixed in. Two sprays. That is enough. My wheat usually gives me about 900 jin per mu, good year maybe 1000 jin.

**Maize after wheat — this is the summer crop.**

After I cut the wheat in June, I will not plow deep. I will just use the small rotary machine — I hire a man with a tractor, 30 yuan per mu, he does it fast. Then I plant hybrid maize seed right away, one seed per hole. Zhengdan type, the one with the red bag. Everyone plants this.

For maize I put compound fertilizer at sowing, one and a half bags per mu. Then when the maize is about knee-high (big bell stage), I put one bag of urea per mu, by hand, next to each plant. That is the way my father taught me and it still works.

Maize I water two times if the rain is not enough — once after sowing if the ground is dry, and once when the tassel comes out. If rain is good I only water once. This area gets summer rain, usually enough.

Pests for maize — I spray once for corn borer when I see the leaves with holes. One spray is usually enough. If army worms come I spray again but most years no.

My maize gives about 1100 jin per mu. Last year was dry in August so I only got 950 jin. I hope this year is better.

I do not change much from year to year. My father farmed this same land, I farm the same way, only the seeds got better and the fertilizer is easier to buy now. Too much change is dangerous when you are old and the land must feed you.
